Why can't some people learn anything new, even from the best teacher?

Kevin Trudeau tells a Zen story. A student demands the secret of enlightenment. The teacher pours tea into his cup until it overflows onto the floor. When the student protests, the master explains that his mind is already full.

Anything poured in will be read through what he already thinks. Kevin says there's no room for the truth until you empty your cup.

What would you have to let go of to learn something new?

Kevin's free training, Your Wish Is Your Command, is in my highlights.

Learning can take 12 minutes or 12 years, depending on one thing.

Kevin Trudeau notes that a normal course of study under a teacher once took 12 years. Today we live in the jet age, so why not learn in 12 minutes?

His answer is that you can, if you have the right attitude. But it can still take a long time to scrub the ego clean, because the mind is covered with so much mud. In the end, the journey, not the destination, is the reward.

Where are you rushing something that needs patience?

How can someone bow down to a person they may be ahead of?

Kevin Trudeau gets asked this when he shows photos of himself with monks and the Dalai Lama. He says the greatest always bow down, humble themselves, and keep filling themselves up. Even Jesus was baptized by John the Baptist.

The axiom behind it is that the wise man learns from the fool, but the fool doesn't learn from the wise man. Kevin asks you to think about that strongly.

Which one are you in your own life?
